Header: Erysiphe polygoni ( Erysiphe betae ) powdery mildew disease

Prevention: Practice crop rotation with non- leguminous crops such as maize and other cereals for a period of one year.
Space 1 ½ ft between rows and ½ ft between plants to increase aeration within the crop
Prune affected leafy vegetation and weed to remove host plants within the farm.
Practice mulching to maintain proper biodiversity and naturally combat invaders.
Avoid watering the plants using overhead systems to reduce spread of disease
Use a slow release organic fertilizer to avoid excess nitrogen as young leafy plant parts are susceptible.
Monitoring: Look out for white powdery patches on leaves and other green parts which later become dull coloured.
Look out for severely infected foliage which is yellow and undergoes premature defoliation
Look out for leaves with necrotic symptoms.
Look out for pods which are reduced in size and turn yellow in colour
Take action when 3 to 4 leaves with grey to white powdery deposits are found on a single plant
Direct Control: Rogue and burn infected plants to reduce spread of disease to healthy plants
Avoid overwatering through overhead irrigation; instead adopt drip irrigation
Jik solution (3 to 5 ml in 1 litre of water) if you have used them on infected plants.
Water early in the morning or after sunset, and try to keep the water on the soil, not the leaves.
Trichoderma harzianum (Trianum-P) at a rate of 15g in 5L or
Trichoderma asperellum (Trichotech) at a rate of 2.5g in 20L of water
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
Start application at onset of disease development ensuring full foliage coverage for excellent control.

Repeat every 7-10 days for as long as needed.
Apply when the first symptoms are observed, with a 10-day application interval.
